name: Prep Calculator
description: Emergency preparedness sums done in plain code, not guessed: water to store and how long it lasts, food energy for a household, battery runtime, a power and solar budget, rough generator fuel, bleach drops for drinking water, and the unit conversions a prepper needs. Answers give US and metric units and name every planning figure used. It works with no internet and stores nothing. Planning figures only, not medical, electrical or engineering advice.
author: Cypher Sisters

tools.water_needed: Work out how much drinking and hygiene water to store for a number of people (and pets) for a number of days, in US gallons and liters, and how many jugs or cans that is.
tools.water_on_hand: Work out how many days the water you have will last for a number of people (and pets).
tools.food_needed: Work out the food energy in kilocalories that adults, children and heavy workers need for a number of days, and roughly how much of one shelf food (rice, dried beans, oats, peanut butter, canned beans) gives that.
tools.battery_runtime: Work out how many hours a battery runs a load, from its watt-hours (or amp-hours and volts), its type and whether the load runs through an inverter.
tools.power_budget: Add up the watt-hours a day for a list of devices, and the battery size and solar panel watts that would cover it.
tools.generator_fuel: Give a rough range of the fuel a small gasoline or propane generator burns for a load and a number of hours, with the carbon monoxide safety line.
tools.bleach_for_water: Work out how many drops of plain unscented household bleach (5 to 9 percent) make clear or cloudy water safer to drink, per public guidance, with the steps that follow.
tools.unit_convert: Convert gallons, liters and quarts; pounds, kilograms, ounces and grams; Fahrenheit and Celsius; miles and kilometers; and watt-hours and amp-hours at a given voltage.
